chapter: La Rocca on who created jazz
title: Rust on writing the Joe Oliver book and Bunk Johnson
summary: Rust explains he edited Walter Allen's interviews and worked from record files, and dismisses Bunk Johnson's recreations as march music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No, I wrote that mostly as a sort of, you might say, editor. Walter Allen managed to interview the various musicians that were still living. And he sent me the facts and I wrote them, sewed them up together. I was more concerned with the records than with the legends. I wasn't very interested in these obscure people from the shadows who were said to have played with this, that and the other musician, in this, that and the other band, and who never made any records at all. I'm not interested in music I can't hear and never will hear, after all. I mean, that's dead. That's dead 60 years ago, and it wasn't very interesting anyway. I've heard some of the recreations, some of these records of Bunk Johnson and people like that who were relying on their memories of what they played. Not only was it not jazz, it was barely ragtime. A lot of it was just simply march music, which may have been all right, but I wish they wouldn't label it jazz. It confuses the issue and it just isn't true. When it came to the book, I dug up the files of the various companies and put the pieces together, supplied by Walter Allen, and he did most of the spade work. I just sewed the thing together, and I also managed to get the book published. That was about as far as I went with it.
